summary: Reconciled the sweep investigation with the newly asserted availability defect rather than leaving the two records side by side. The sweep's own event set is what produced the three apply-side rejections behind the defect (CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad indices 17-19), yet the four invariants it checks reported no violation there, because none of them covers whether a committed configuration change is admissible at the node that must apply it - that is a real gap in what the sweep measures, not a contradiction in its results. I registered it as a necessary question under the sweep investigation, naming what a check would have to observe (for each applied EntryConfChangeV2: that it is accepted, that the tracker state before and after is consistent with it, and that no node applies an entry its own state rejects) and asking whether that property can be stated without re-implementing the target's admission logic. No experiment was requested, since such a check belongs with the deterministic prefix already registered on @joint_apply_order rather than with another randomized run. Current state of the run: four questions carry terminal interpretations (campaign admission guard explained and refuted; ReadIndex loss across a term change explained and refuted; transfer delay bounded and holding; joint-change ordering explained then narrowed to an asserted availability defect), the joint-apply investigation is the one live thread with an asserted defect claim backed by a receipt and a source-level mechanism hypothesis awaiting its deterministic prefix, and the sweep's remaining open item is this newly registered measurement gap plus the earlier unanswered part of its gap about demotion and restarts.
